entities.summary: Malik al-Ashtar, romanized: Mālik al-Ashtar), born Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith al-Nakhaʿī al-Madhḥijī, was an Arab military commander and tribal leader of the Nakha branch of the Madhhij confederation. A prominent figure during the Rashidun Caliphate, he is best known as the most loyal and formidable general of the fourth Caliph, Ali ibn Abi Talib. In Kufa, Malik emerged as a leader of the opposition against Caliph Uthman, playing a key role in the events leading to the Caliph's death. Following the election of Ali, he became the Caliph’s most trusted general and strategist during the First Fitna, holding senior commands at the battles of the Camel and Siffin.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a trusted general and strategist of Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib during the First Fitna, Malik al-Ashtar played a crucial role in shaping the outcome of the battles of the Camel and Siffin. His leadership significantly impacted the fate of the Rashidun Caliphate.
